fixes.explanation: A promise from the LORD sounds lovely, friend, and I'd read that stone all day. But that's not what's on it. Verse 14 says each stone was engraved like a seal with "…the name of one of the twelve tribes." (Exodus 39:14) Picture the engraver: twelve stones, twelve names, and not one spelling mistake allowed. I'd be sweating through my apron.

A line from the law is a fair guess, friend, but that's not what the engraver carved. Verse 14 says each of the twelve stones was "…engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes." (Exodus 39:14) A name on every stone, one tribe each. Honestly, if I had to engrave twelve of anything, I'd stamp them crooked and call it art.

True, and look at that finish! The crown's plate gets its blue cord in verse 31. Then verse 32 says, "So all the work for the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, was completed." (Exodus 39:32) That's the whole to-do list, done. I haven't finished a to-do list since the junk drawer days, and nobody was even assigning me one then.
